readings: Link each invoice line item to its order through its invoice (`Invoices.order_id`), and from the order to the customer's town or city. First, for each order item id and town, average the line `product_price` and the ratio `derived_product_cost` / `derived_total_cost`, ignoring missing values. Then, for each town, average those per-item averages. Show the towns whose average cost ratio is above the average of that ratio across all towns, with the town, its average price, its average ratio, and how much its ratio exceeds the cross-town average. No rounding.
queries:
WITH item_town AS (
  SELECT ili.order_item_id,
         c.town_city AS town,
         AVG(ili.product_price) AS avg_price,
         AVG(ili.derived_product_cost * 1.0 / ili.derived_total_cost) AS avg_ratio
  FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili
  JOIN Invoices i ON ili.invoice_number = i.invoice_number
  JOIN Orders o ON i.order_id = o.order_id
  JOIN Customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  GROUP BY ili.order_item_id, c.town_city
),
town_stats AS (
  SELECT town,
         AVG(avg_price) AS avg_price,
         AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_ratio
  FROM item_town
  GROUP BY town
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS overall_ratio FROM town_stats
)
SELECT t.town,
       t.avg_price,
       t.avg_ratio,
       t.avg_ratio - o.overall_ratio AS ratio_excess
FROM town_stats t, overall o
WHERE t.avg_ratio > o.overall_ratio;
